html:
Tecumseh was a Shawnee leader who tried to unite the Native nations of the Great Lakes and the South against the advance of American settlers. He said no nation could sell land that belonged to all.

With his brother Tenskwatawa, called the Prophet, he built a village at Prophetstown in Indiana and travelled south to win allies. In 1811, while he was away, American troops under William Henry Harrison destroyed it at the Battle of Tippecanoe.

In the War of 1812 Tecumseh allied with the British and helped take Detroit. He was killed at the Battle of the Thames in Upper Canada in 1813, and his confederacy fell apart, opening the way for Indian removal.
